title: The Blowing of the Horn and Two Records

paragraphs.text: The surah asks whether anyone can now see any trace remaining of those destroyed nations, whose homes once stood strong. None of them is left. Pharaoh, the peoples before him and the overturned cities also committed sin and disobeyed the messenger sent by their Lord, so Allah seized them with an extremely severe grip. When the flood waters rose high, Allah carried the ancestors of humanity in the sailing ship. He did this so that the event would become a reminder, and so that ears which listen with attention would remember it and keep it.

The surah then describes the end of the world. The Horn will be blown, and a single blast will be enough. The earth and the mountains will be lifted up and crushed flat with one blow. On that Day, the great Event will take place. The sky will split apart, because on that Day it will be weak and fragile. The angels will stand at its edges, and eight of them will carry the Throne of the Lord above them. On that Day, every person will be presented for judgement, and not one secret will stay hidden, no matter how carefully it was concealed before.

Whoever receives his record in his right hand will be filled with joy and will say to others, "Here, come and read my record!" He will explain that during his life he was always sure that he would one day meet his account and stand before his Lord. He will enjoy a pleasant, satisfying life in a high and lofty garden, where clusters of fruit hang low and are easy to pick. The people there will be told to eat and drink happily, as a reward for the good deeds they sent ahead in the days that have passed.

But whoever receives his record in his left hand will speak with deep regret. He will cry that he wishes he had never been given his record at all. His sorrow on that Day stands in sharp contrast to the joy of the one who received his record in his right hand.

hardWords.m: a very small sign that something was there
people in your family who lived long ago
